lead: Des Moines plumbing deals with deep cold, hard river water, basements and older homes. PipeMend sends licensed local plumbers across Des Moines.
risk: frozen pipes, lead and galvanized service lines and basement backups
risk_short: frozen pipes, old lines and basement backups
why: Sherman Hill, Drake, Beaverdale and Highland Park have homes from the 1890s to the 1940s with galvanized supply lines, cast-iron stacks and lead service lines in some cases.
Winters freeze pipes near exterior walls. Heavy rain and river flooding, as in 1993 and 2008, back water into basements in low areas.
water: Des Moines Water Works treats water from the Raccoon and Des Moines rivers and shallow wells. It is hard. The utility runs a nitrate removal system when farm runoff raises river levels.
tips: Keep the heat on and cabinets open in deep cold.
Ask the water works about your service line material.
Test your sump pump each spring.
areas: PipeMend works in Sherman Hill, Drake, Beaverdale, Waterbury, the East Village, Highland Park, South of Grand and every other neighborhood.
permits: Plumbing permits come from the City of Des Moines Permit and Development Center, and plumbers must be licensed by the Iowa Plumbing and Mechanical Systems Board.

faq.a: Yes. Water from the Raccoon and Des Moines rivers carries a lot of minerals. Scale builds up in water heaters and on fixtures, so many homes use softeners.
